solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Our group are going to fuss? That's rich

parts.note: our group is 'we', and 'are going to' is 'will', so together WE'LL with the apostrophe dropped
a to-do is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud whether their crowd fussing makes them wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase reads as a sentence but contracts to WE'LL; the apostrophe is ignored, as usual in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-to-do is prosperous and comfortably off, a synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: Playing more tennis — soup provided

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of 'more tennis' are being toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: More tennis is played, with soup laid on for the players.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup, so this is an example of the category.

clue.text: Untidy place to sleep — made fun of learner inside

parts.note: a bed is a place to sleep

indicators.note: inside says the learner's letter goes within the word for made fun of

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them, so ragged means made fun of
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A messy bed, and a learner was mocked while in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled describes someone dishevelled and messy-looking, a synonym for scruffy.

clue.text: Love being entertained by favourite writer

indicators.note: being entertained by means held as a guest within, so the love letter sits inside the word for favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance enjoyed by a well-loved author.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet is a writer of verse, so this is a specific kind of author.

clue.text: Latest from all directions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the most recent information
second meaning, cryptically: the four compass points north, east, west and south, abbreviated ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading spells the word out of the compass-point abbreviations, a folk etymology for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest is the most recent information, which is what news means; and the compass initials spell it.

clue.text: Reminder to ring Liberal — one of 30 here

indicators.note: to ring means to encircle, so the word for reminder surrounds the Liberal letter

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder, as given to an actor

explanation.surface: A prompt to telephone a Liberal politician, apparently one of thirty people.
explanation.walkthrough: The 30 is not a cross-reference to another entry: this puzzle has thirty clues, and the answer is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: This grid has thirty clues in all, and each is a prompt the solver works from, so the answer is one of them.

clue.text: Boating facility steep — daughter, English, leaving

indicators.note: leaving says those two letters depart from the word for steep

parts.note: to marinade food is to steep it in a liquid
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A harbour with a steep approach, which a daughter and an Englishman leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour with moorings for yachts and pleasure craft.

clue.text: With power for time, give detailed account of method to achieve objective

indicators.note: 'power for time' means the power letter stands in place of the time letter

parts.note: to recite is to relate or enumerate in detail
T is the physics symbol for time
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Reads like a management instruction to explain one's strategy in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a recipe is a formula for producing a result, as in a recipe for success.

clue.text: Too much to bear — finished with fellow keeping nothing inside

parts.note: over means ended or finished

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the word for fellow holds the zero letter
inside confirms the nothing letter goes within the fellow word

parts.note: a lad is a fellow or young man
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: An exhausted man has finished, with nothing left in him.
explanation.definitionFit: An overload is an excessive burden, more than a load can stand.

clue.text: Unaccompanied part song leading to merriment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a song for three or more voices without instruments

explanation.surface: A cappella singing that leads to general jollity.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical sense of glee is an English choral form, mainly 18th century; 'leading to' just joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word names both a choral composition for unaccompanied voices and a feeling of joyful delight.

clue.text: Nasty stories, praise oddly lacking, for meat shop

indicators.note: nasty means the stories have gone bad, so their letters get rearranged
oddly lacking means the odd-numbered letters of praise are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Unpleasant tales lacking praise circulate about a butcher's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly lacking' drops the first, third and fifth letters of 'praise', keeping the even ones; that tail is added after the rearranged stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie can be a restaurant or shop selling meat roasted on a rotating spit.

clue.text: Favouring introduction of troops in defensive position

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it

indicators.note: introduction of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone backs sending soldiers to a stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A fort is a fortified military building held against attack.

clue.text: Language expert's anagram — I'm at first really at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled
at first means the opening letter of really

explanation.surface: A linguist admits being baffled by an anagram.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue cheekily uses the word 'anagram' as its own fodder; ''s' joins the definition to the wordplay as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammarian is a specialist in the structure and rules of a tongue.

clue.text: High mark, high point, that's out of bounds

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain or peak

indicators.note: out of bounds means the bounding letters at each end are removed, leaving the inside

parts.note: read as 'that is', the word that

explanation.surface: A top grade, a summit, that is off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' stands for 'is', so the fodder is THAT with its outer Ts stripped, giving HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the top grade in some marking schemes, as in alpha plus for excellent work.

clue.text: Philosopher bringing up Greek character — in northeast for long period

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher

indicators.note: bringing up in a down clue means the following pieces are read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
NE is the compass abbreviation for northeast

explanation.surface: A philosopher raising a Greek figure in the northeast for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A millennium is a span of a thousand years, a very lengthy stretch of time.

clue.text: Agent very much recalled by one politician in safekeeping facility

parts.note: a rep, a representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for very much is read backwards

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so tired'
I is the Roman numeral one
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An agent, called back by a politician, is kept in secure storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a place where things are stored or deposited for safety.

clue.text: Musical piece from basso, lovely

indicators.note: piece from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Praise for a song performed by a fine bass singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical piece' looks like the definition, but 'piece from' is the hiding signal and 'Musical' alone defines, as an adjective-turned-noun for a musical performance by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo is a performance by a single musician, so here a musical turn by one person.

clue.text: Part of jacket, article from Paris friend shows on return

indicators.note: on return means the combined pieces are read back the other way

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A French friend shows off part of a jacket on coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded flap on the front of a coat or jacket below the collar.

clue.text: By the sound of it, full agreement

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for full is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: packed means full, as a packed room

explanation.surface: Apparently there is complete consensus.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal treaty or deal between parties.

clue.text: A cash win, unexpected, used for tool

indicators.note: unexpected says the letters turn up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A surprise cash prize is spent on equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a motorised cutting implement with teeth on a loop of chain.

clue.text: Shabby group embracing publicity suspension

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the group word holds the other pieces

parts.note: three can mean a group of three, a trio
an ad is publicity, an advertisement
a bar is a ban or suspension, as in a bar on trading

explanation.surface: A tatty band welcomes a publicity ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare clothing is worn thin and shabby, the nap rubbed away.

clue.text: Describing animal-lover's stockings? About right, snazzy ultimately

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing a lover of one particular animal

indicators.note: about means around, so the stockings word goes around the right letter

parts.note: hose is a collective word for stockings

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Asks whether an equestrian's hosiery is right and smart.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: horse-lovers' stockings could be called by the adjective that describes their owners.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsey people are devoted to horses and riding, so the adjective fits an equestrian enthusiast.

clue.text: After reflection criticises Pole

indicators.note: after reflection means seen in a mirror, so the letters appear backwards

parts.note: to rap is to criticise sharply

explanation.surface: A Polish person criticises after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but here it is a wooden pole, as on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole such as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: Sure, can act to reform shrimp, say

indicators.note: to reform means to form again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doubtful voice agrees someone can act in a reformist way about shrimps.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp is one example of a hard-shelled aquatic arthropod, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Foam steams up rather fast initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Froth bubbles up very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Surf is the white froth of breaking waves on the shore.

clue.text: Half of letters — subject of significant split?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptically: the first half of the alphabet, A to M, written out as three words
second meaning: the particle whose splitting was a landmark of physics

explanation.surface: Half the alphabet is the subject of a momentous division.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: splitting the atom was a turning point of 20th-century physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting the nucleus was a momentous scientific feat, so this particle is what underwent the famous division.

clue.text: Sword set piece used on regular basis

indicators.note: used on a regular basis means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A sword is used routinely in a staged set piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing blade with a stiff triangular cross-section.

clue.text: Very small home is new centre for plaything

indicators.note: is new centre for means the home word replaces the middle letter of the plaything word

parts.note: a toy is a plaything
in means at home

explanation.surface: A tiny house becomes the new hub for a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny means minute or extremely little.

clue.text: Exotic fare a few find dreadful

indicators.note: exotic means foreign or strange, so the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: some means a few, an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Several diners find foreign food frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome means frightening or alarming, a synonym for terrible.

clue.text: Turmoil ahead, river blade needed

parts.note: up means ahead, as in a team two goals up
R is the map abbreviation for river
an oar's flat end is its blade, so blade stands for the oar

explanation.surface: Trouble upstream as a rower needs a new oar.
explanation.definitionFit: Uproar is noisy commotion and disorder.
